prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1130; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle struck the rear of the insured vehicle at low speed. Police report requested. Claimant has retained counsel, who has requested that all communications be directed to the firm going forward.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office. Confirmed representation and received the signed letter of representation. Requested medical authorization forms and the names of all treating providers. Counsel indicated the claimant has complained of neck pain and stiffness since the collision and has begun physical therapy.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos of both vehicles submitted by the insured. Rear bumper damage to the insured vehicle is visible, with minor deformation to the rear panel. Photos of the claimant vehicle show a cracked taillight and a scuffed front bumper. Vehicle appraisal ordered for both sides.

Entry 4: Received initial treatment records from the claimant's chiropractor. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain with muscle spasm. Records indicate the claimant reported neck pain rated as moderate and limited range of motion. No fractures or imaging-confirmed injuries noted at this stage. Follow-up records requested through counsel.

Entry 5: Status review with supervisor. Liability appears probable against the other driver based on the police report and the rear-end nature of the impact. Claim remains open pending final treatment records, the vehicle appraisal, and a demand package from counsel. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days.
